es.summary: Formaciones de tejido cicatricial que unen órganos o paredes abdominales, pudiendo causar obstrucción intestinal o infertilidad.
key_points: Se forman tras cirugía abdominal o inflamación pélvica.
Pueden ser asintomáticas o producir obstrucción parcial/completa.
No existen pruebas diagnósticas específicas; se detectan en cirugía o imágenes de obstrucción.
Manejo conservador incluye dieta baja en fibra y control de líquidos.
Complicaciones graves: isquemia intestinal, perforación y infertilidad femenina.

pathophysiology: Lesión peritoneal desencadena inflamación y liberación de fibroblastos.
Depósito de colágeno forma bandas fibrosas entre superficies serosas.
Las adherencias limitan el deslizamiento normal de intestinos y órganos.
Obstrucción ocurre cuando la luz intestinal se estrecha o se torce.
signs_symptoms: Distensión y ausencia de gases o heces.
Infertilidad en mujeres con adherencias pélvicas.
diagnostics: Radiografía de abdomen: asas dilatadas y niveles aire‑líquido.
Tomografía axial computarizada: localiza sitio y grado de obstrucción.
Ecografía pélvica para evaluar adherencias en infertilidad.
treatment: Manejo conservador: hidratación IV, dieta baja en fibra, analgesia.
Antieméticos (ondansetrón) y laxantes suaves si es necesario.
Cirugía de adhesiolisis cuando hay obstrucción completa o dolor crónico.
Uso de barreras antiadherentes (hialuronato) en cirugía preventiva.
complications: Obstrucción intestinal completa → isquemia y perforación.
Deshidratación y desequilibrio electrolítico por vómitos.
Infertilidad por bloqueo de trompas de Falopio.
nursing_care: Evaluar abdomen: dolor, distensión, ruidos intestinales.
Monitorear signos vitales y balance hídrico cada 4 h.
Mantener NGT en posición adecuada si está indicada.
Administrar analgésicos y antieméticos según prescripción.
Preparar al paciente para posible cirugía y explicar el procedimiento.
patient_teaching: Seguir dieta baja en fibra y aumentar líquidos claros.
Reconocer signos de obstrucción: dolor intenso, vómitos persistentes, ausencia de gases.
Importancia de acudir a control postoperatorio para detectar adherencias.
Opciones de fertilidad y derivación a ginecología si hay infertilidad.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
related_to: Pérdida de líquidos por obstrucción intestinal
outcomes: Balance hídrico: mantener ingesta y salida de líquidos dentro de ±500 mL/24 h
Peso corporal: mantener peso estable (±0.5 kg) durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar déficit temprano y guiar la reposición de fluidos

interventions.action: Administrar solución cristaloide IV según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Reemplaza pérdidas y previene hipovolemia

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de deshidratación (turgencia cutánea, mucosas secas)
interventions.rationale: Identifica rápidamente la necesidad de intervención

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos claros en pequeñas cantidades frecuentes
interventions.rationale: Facilita la tolerancia y reduce el riesgo de vómitos

interventions.action: Monitorear presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios hemodinámicos por pérdida de volumen

outcomes: Niveles séricos de Na⁺ y K⁺ dentro de rango normal (Na 135‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L)
Ausencia de síntomas neurológicos de desequilibrio (confusión, debilidad muscular)

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar electrolitos séricos al ingreso y cada 24 h
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar alteraciones y ajustar la terapia

interventions.action: Administrar solución electrolítica IV según orden médica
interventions.rationale: Corrige déficit de sodio y potasio de forma controlada

interventions.action: Evaluar estado neurológico y fuerza muscular cada turno
interventions.rationale: Detecta signos tempranos de hipocalemia o hipernatremia

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre alimentos ricos en potasio (plátano, papaya) cuando sea apropiado
interventions.rationale: Apoya la reposición natural de electrolitos

interventions.action: Documentar cualquier episodio de vómitos o diarrea y su duración
interventions.rationale: Facilita correlación con cambios en electrolitos

en.summary: Scar tissue formations that unite organs or abdominal walls, potentially causing intestinal obstruction or infertility.
key_points: Form after abdominal surgery or pelvic inflammation.
May be asymptomatic or cause partial/complete obstruction.
No specific diagnostic tests; detected during surgery or imaging of obstruction.
Conservative management includes low-fiber diet and fluid control.
Severe complications: intestinal ischemia, perforation, and female infertility.

pathophysiology: Peritoneal injury triggers inflammation and fibroblast release.
Collagen deposition forms fibrous bands between serosal surfaces.
Adhesions restrict normal sliding of intestines and organs.
Obstruction occurs when the intestinal lumen narrows or twists.
risk_factors: Invasive procedures such as prolonged laparoscopy.
signs_symptoms: Intermittent abdominal pain or colicky pain.
Distension and absence of flatus or stool.
Infertility in women with pelvic adhesions.
diagnostics: Abdominal X‑ray: dilated loops and air‑fluid levels.
CT scan: localizes site and degree of obstruction.
Pelvic ultrasound to evaluate adhesions in infertility.
treatment: Conservative management: IV hydration, low‑fiber diet, analgesia.
Antiemetics (ondansetron) and mild laxatives if needed.
Adhesiolysis surgery when complete obstruction or chronic pain present.
Use of anti‑adhesion barriers (hyaluronate) in preventive surgery.
complications: Complete intestinal obstruction → ischemia and perforation.
Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance from vomiting.
nursing_care: Assess abdomen: pain, distension, bowel sounds.
Monitor vital signs and fluid balance every 4 h.
Maintain NG tube in proper position if indicated.
Administer analgesics and antiemetics per prescription.
Prepare patient for possible surgery and explain the procedure.
patient_teaching: Follow low‑fiber diet and increase clear fluids.
Recognize signs of obstruction: severe pain, persistent vomiting, no flatus.
Importance of postoperative follow‑up to detect adhesions.
Fertility options and referral to gynecology if infertility present.

outcomes: Fluid balance: maintain intake and output within ±500 mL/24 h
Body weight: maintain stable weight (±0.5 kg) during hospitalization

interventions.action: Record intake and output every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of deficit and guides fluid replacement

interventions.action: Administer crystalloid IV solution per prescription
interventions.rationale: Replaces losses and prevents hypovolemia

interventions.action: Assess for dehydration signs (skin turgor, dry mucous membranes)
interventions.rationale: Rapidly identifies need for intervention

interventions.action: Offer clear fluids in small frequent amounts
interventions.rationale: Facilitates tolerance and reduces vomiting risk

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detects hemodynamic changes from volume loss

outcomes: Serum Na⁺ and K⁺ levels within normal range (Na 135‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L)
Absence of neurological symptoms of imbalance (confusion, muscle weakness)

interventions.action: Obtain and record serum electrolytes at admission and every 24 h
interventions.rationale: Identifies alterations and adjusts therapy

interventions.action: Administer IV electrolyte solution per order
interventions.rationale: Corrects sodium and potassium deficits in a controlled manner

interventions.action: Assess neurological status and muscle strength each shift
interventions.rationale: Detects early signs of hypokalemia or hypernatremia

interventions.action: Educate patient on potassium‑rich foods (banana, papaya) when appropriate
interventions.rationale: Supports natural electrolyte replenishment

interventions.action: Document any vomiting or diarrhea episodes and duration
interventions.rationale: Facilitates correlation with electrolyte changes

summary.0.quote: Adhesions are bands of scar-like tissue.

key_points.0.quote: The risk factors for developing a hydrosalpinx are the same as for a tubal blockage, including infection, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), and scar tissue or adhesions from prior abdominal surgery (Yao et al., 2023).

key_points.1.quote: If they partly block your intestines, a diet low in fiber can allow food to move easily through the affected area.

key_points.2.quote: No tests are available to detect adhesions.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Normally, internal tissues and organs have slippery surfaces so they can shift easily as the body moves.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: These blockages can result from several factors, including: infection inflammation scar tissue from endometriosis or previous pelvic or abdominal surgery adhesions structural issues (Roberts, 2023)

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Adhesions can sometimes cause infertility in women by preventing fertilized eggs from reaching the uterus.

sections.treatment.2.quote: If you have a complete intestinal obstruction, it is life-threatening. You should get immediate medical attention and may need surgery.

sections.complications.2.quote: Like a blockage from scar tissue, it causes difficulty for the movement of both sperm and egg and results in infertility ( Figure 4.15 ).

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: If they partly block your intestines, a diet low in fiber can allow food to move easily through the affected area.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: But when they partly or completely block the intestines , they cause symptoms such as: Severe abdominal pain or cramping Vomiting Bloating An inability to pass gas Constipation
